claims.text: A CustomResourceDefinition adds a new kind to the API server; once the CRD is Established, the API server serves the kind and kubectl apply, get and delete work on its objects like built-in objects.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Tasks > Extend the Kubernetes API with CustomResourceDefinitions (Create a CustomResourceDefinition; Create custom objects)

claims.text: The API server stores a CRD and the custom resources of its kind in etcd, as it does for built-in objects.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Extending the Kubernetes API > Custom Resources (CustomResourceDefinitions; storage)

claims.text: Adding a CRD needs no rebuild or restart of the API server: custom resources appear and disappear in a running cluster through dynamic registration, and a CRD contains no program.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Custom Resources ('dynamic registration'; 'CRDs do not require programming')

claims.text: Argo CD's Application, Sealed Secrets' SealedSecret and MetalLB's IPAddressPool are custom resources whose CRDs come in each project's install manifest; the Sealed Secrets controller turns each SealedSecret into a Secret.
claims.source_hint: argo-cd docs: Declarative Setup (Application CRD); sealed-secrets README (SealedSecret CRD, controller); metallb.io Installation by manifest; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/custom-resources.txt

claims.text: On donhang, kubectl get crds lists nine CRDs whose names end in metallb.io, including ipaddresspools.metallb.io; the script prints names only (custom-columns=NAME).

A CRD's metadata.name must be <plural>.<group>, here backuppolicies.donhang.example; backuppolicies is the lowercase plural of the kind, used by the commands; the API group is the part of apiVersion before the slash, the version (v1alpha1) the part after it.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Extend the Kubernetes API with CustomResourceDefinitions (example CRD comment 'name must match the spec fields below, and be in the form: <plural>.<group>'); API Overview > API groups

claims.text: A CRD itself is not namespaced (cluster-wide); with scope: Namespaced each of its objects lives in a namespace; kubectl api-resources --api-group=donhang.example lists backuppolicies, donhang.example/v1alpha1, NAMESPACED true, kind BackupPolicy.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: CRD task page L31-36 ('CustomResourceDefinitions themselves are non-namespaced'; scope Namespaced or Cluster); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/custom-resources.txt

claims.text: The API server validates a custom resource against the CRD's openAPIV3Schema on create and update and refuses one that breaks it; retentionDays: seven is refused with 'must be of type integer', and a quoted YAML value such as "7" is a string, so it fails type: integer too.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: CRD task page > Validation; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/custom-resources.txt; YAML 1.2 spec (quoted scalars are strings)

claims.text: The schema makes claimName, schedule and retentionDays required, retentionDays an integer of at least 1, and schedule only a string: with no pattern, the API server does not check cron syntax. Cron 0 2 * * * means every day at 02:00.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: CRD task page > Validation (OpenAPI v3: type, required, minimum, pattern); backup-policy-crd.yaml lines 34-44 @ stage-3; kubernetes.io: CronJob > Schedule syntax

claims.text: The API server records conditions (named statuses) on a CRD; Established turns true once its kind is served; custom-resources.sh waits for it with kubectl wait --for=condition=Established before listing the kind.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: CRD task page (status conditions, Established); scripts/k8s/custom-resources.sh line 23 @ stage-3

claims.text: A Deployment leads to Pods because a control loop in the control plane watches Deployments and creates ReplicaSets for them.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Controllers; Workloads > Deployments; Components > kube-controller-manager

claims.text: Without a controller watching its kind, a custom resource is only stored and read back: ten seconds after db-nightly is created, operator-lessons has no Job and no Pod.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Custom Resources ('On their own, custom resources let you store and retrieve structured data'; Custom controllers); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/custom-resources.txt

claims.text: Deleting a CRD removes its kind from the API and deletes every custom resource of that kind in every namespace; afterwards kubectl get backuppolicies returns NotFound, not an empty list.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: CRD task page > Delete a CustomResourceDefinition ('delete all custom objects stored in it'); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/custom-resources.txt last lines

claims.text: A chart can keep CRDs in a crds/ folder apart from its templates; Helm installs them on helm install, skipping any that already exist, and does not upgrade or delete them; Helm's docs give unintended data loss as the reason.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh: Chart Best Practices > Custom Resource Definitions ('Some Caveats (and Explanations)'); Topics > Charts (crds directory)

claims.text: Argo CD renders a chart itself with helm template (renders manifests, installs nothing) and by default includes the chart's CRDs in the manifests it compares and syncs, unlike helm upgrade; a new chart version's CRD changes appear in the Application's diff.
claims.source_hint: argo-cd docs release-3.1: User Guide > Helm ('Helm is only used to inflate charts with helm template'; skipCrds); Sync Options

claims.text: Traefik's Helm chart brings its own kinds, such as IngressRoute (Traefik's kind for routing rules), as CRDs, which Argo CD syncs with the chart pinned in apps/traefik.yaml.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/gitops/config-repo/apps/traefik.yaml syncOptions comment @ stage-3; doc.traefik.io Kubernetes CRD provider; Traefik Helm chart crds/

claims.text: When objects of a chart's CRD kinds exist, read the CRD changes in the diff of a new chart version first, because the API server checks every later create or update of those objects against the changed schema.
claims.source_hint: outline item 6; follows from claims 8 and 13-15 (schema validated on creation and updates: CRD task page L665)

claims.text: custom-resources.sh runs on the host against donhang and installs MetalLB first when metallb-system is missing; show prints a command before running it; 2>&1 || true keeps an error's text in the output and lets the script continue.
claims.source_hint: scripts/k8s/custom-resources.sh lines 3, 8 @ stage-3; scripts/lib/network-lessons.sh line 5 @ stage-3; bash manual (Redirections; Lists of Commands)
